text: AI is expected to grow in importance for pig breeding since it's the best way to bring good genetics into a village and reduces disease transmission risk compared to moving a boar between farms. Doses are prepared at a dedicated AI center, which requires experience and equipment; insemination of females can be done by a veterinarian, VAHW, or a briefly trained farmer. Semen collection: boars are trained to mount a heavy dummy sow; once mounted and excited, the technician catches and disinfects the penis, then massages it until ejaculation, collecting the sperm through a filter (called 'tapioca') that removes dirt and solids. Dose preparation: sperm concentration and motility are checked under a microscope, then diluted with BTS extender (providing nutrients for longer conservation and antibiotics against bacterial contamination); doses of 100 ml containing about 1 billion spermatozoa are packaged. Transport/storage: semen can be kept 2 days at an AI center in a fridge holding a stable 16°C; when transporting to a farm, use ice to keep it cold but never let the semen contact the ice directly. Insemination timing: detect immobility (standing heat) in the sow/gilt; inseminate gilts 12 hours after detecting immobility and sows 24 hours after; a second insemination about 12 hours after the first is recommended.
